# dsh-better-plugin-updater
**English** | 简体中文
Check for and install updates to your DeepSeek Harness plugins, without leaving DSH.
It uses DSH's plugin manager to change packages. Open a GitHub-sourced plugin's detail page to check
and review its update, or use the commands below. npm registry packages keep DSH's native update co
ntrols. Updates never run without your confirmation.
## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later.
- A managed DSH profile, in the Web app, the desktop app or the terminal.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package is published to npm, so this fetches a bundle that is already built: the install runs no
build step and needs no toolchain on this machine. Its own dependencies need no install scripts eit
her, though a profile policy can still prompt for other packages.
Replace `web` with the profile you use. Then refresh an already-open Web page so the browser half lo
ace `web` with the profile you use. Then refresh an already-open Web page so the browser half loads.
Installing from the repository works too, but that source holds no built files, so the install has t
o build the bundle and may ask you to approve that step:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
To remove it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
If the update commands do not appear after a refresh, restart DSH once. DSH remembers that an instal
led package had no browser code, and an installation that was already running without the browser ha
lf keeps that cached answer until DSH starts again. A fresh installation does not hit this.
## Use
### Update from a plugin's page
Open Plugins and then the detail page of a plugin you installed from GitHub. A Version section appea
rs under its source information and checks for an update as soon as the page opens. It shows the cur
rent commit or version against the exact target, and the update runs only after you accept the risk
in the confirmation dialog.
This section is for plugins installed from a GitHub repository or a GitHub release tarball. npm regi
stry packages keep DSH's own version control, and a linked or local plugin has no update source to c
packages keep DSH's own version control, and a linked or local plugin has no update source to check.
### Use the commands
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Updates are never applied until you confirm them. `/plugin-updater update foo bar` accepts several p
ackages at once, and `*` or `?` match package names. Repeating the command, or sending `ok` or `conf
irm`, performs the update you were just shown.
If you already know what you want and accept the risk described below:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Choose a language
Commands follow your interface language. To force one:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Let the agent check for you
The same checks are available to the agent as the read-only `plugin_updates` tool. It can list bundl
es and check for updates, but it cannot install updates, accept the removal risk, approve a build sc
ript or grant a compatibility exemption. Updates require your confirmation in the detail page or a s
a compatibility exemption. Updates require your confirmation in the detail page or a slash command.
## What it can check
| Where the plugin comes from | How an update is found |

| npm | The highest stable version in your registry. Downgrades are never proposed. |
| A Git reposi

tory | The newest commit on the tracked branch, compared with the commit you installed. |
| A GitHub

release | The highest version tag, prereleases included. GitHub's "latest" marker is ignored. |
| A
local folder, or anything else | Reported as unsupported rather than guessed at. |
Fixed npm versions and GitHub source commits remain protected from updates. Use `/plugin-updater upd
ate foo --allow-pinned` to authorize one update and confirm it normally, or set `allowPinned` in the
configuration for ongoing authorization. A fixed Git commit is compared with the repository's defau
lt branch unless `sources.foo.ref` selects a ref. Use `/plugin-updater update foo --allow-pinned --g
it-branch feature/name` to select a branch for one operation. With several packages, the branch appl
ies to each GitHub source package. The selected branch may not contain the installed commit, so revi
ew the exact target before confirming. `--allow-pinned` and `--git-branch` cannot be combined with `
--accept-removal-risk`, and the newly installed target remains pinned. See configuration.
DSH's own bundles and protected packages are skipped. This plugin can check its own supported instal
lation source, but it cannot update itself. Use an external method appropriate for its source. A loc
al linked installation is not supported by the update checker.
## Risks
**An update is not atomic.** The old package is removed before the new one is installed. If the inst
all then fails, or the package needs a build script you have not approved, the package can be left m
issing. A recovery target is printed whenever one is known, but recovery is manual and there is no a
target is printed whenever one is known, but recovery is manual and there is no automatic rollback.
For a package from an npm registry, the new version and its dependencies are downloaded before the o
ld package is removed, so the installation itself needs no network. If that download fails, the upda
te stops and the installed package stays as it is. GitHub sources and release tarballs are not downl
oaded in advance, so those updates still need a network connection when the installation runs.
This plugin never approves build scripts and never grants a compatibility exemption for you.
## Configuration
Most settings have a form in DSH's plugin settings page. Open the plugin's entry there, edit the fie
lds and press Save, and the new value applies the next time the plugin uses it, without a restart. T
he form's labels follow your interface language. `sources` and `indexes` are set in the profile patc
h, because a nested per-package override is not a form field.
Every field is optional.
| Field | Default | Purpose |

| `language` | `auto` | `auto`, `en` or `zh`. `auto` follows your interface language. |
| `sources`

| empty | Per-package overrides, described below. |
| `githubTokenEnv` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | The creden

tial reference to resolve. Not a token value. |
| `requestTimeoutMs` | `15000` | Deadline for one me

tadata request. |
| `maxMetadataBytes` | `4194304` | Largest metadata response accepted, in bytes. |
| `planTtlMs` | `600000` | How long a confirmation stays valid. |
